cards.title: Analyte, Matrix, and Unit Definitions for Descriptive Data
cards.claim: Concentration data must be labeled with the specific matrix (e.g., plasma, serum, tissue homogenate) and analyte identity (parent, metabolite, or specific component of a mixture). Units must specify mass/volume or mass/tissue-mass. Total and free bases are distinct; whole-lung homogenate is not equivalent to epithelial lining fluid (ELF).
conditions: Applicable when cataloging raw concentration-time data for EDA.
Requires explicit distinction between administered dose basis (e.g., salt vs. free base) and measured analyte.
Source-specific numbers (e.g., LLOQ) are not universal thresholds but define the assay's quantifiable range.
required_inputs: Provenance: Source ID and chunk ID for each data point.
Identity: Exact analyte or component identity versus total mixture, with matrix type.
Units: Explicit mass/volume (e.g., mg/L) or mass/tissue-mass (e.g., µg/g) with total/free basis.
Time: Documented time origin (e.g., dose start) and units.
limitations: Group means cannot be treated as individual trajectories.
Technical replicates do not increase biological n.
BLQ is not zero; missing/not-sampled/technical failure are distinct states.
Abstract-only evidence cannot support unreported method details.
cards.downstream_use: Enables valid comparison of exposure metrics (AUC, Cmax) by ensuring denominator and basis consistency. Prevents invalid pooling of incompatible matrices or analytes.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Dose/event/time, analyte, matrix, units and free/total concentration definitions attached to descriptive evidence

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
